claims.criterionText: On the fixture, an effect the signal graph carries produces a finding naming that effect — by its graph label when the graph supplies one, and otherwise by the edge the graph records for it — together with the signals the graph's edges say it reads, and naming nothing the graph does not carry.
claims.reason: The criterion is scoped to the fixture by its own opening clause, and its facts are the join's answer for the counter page's signal graph, which no insurance-portal route renders: CHARTER.md's portal clause reaches a feature only where a portal route can produce the facts, and the surface that shows this finding is the panel served from apps/angular-ai-devtools, not a portal page. Measured at this head in research/raw/m039-render-phase.json: the effect is node 5 of six, kind 'effect', label "", epoch 1, one edge to signal:count, and the join answers namedBy 'recorded-edge' with reads ["count"]. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/render-phase.test.mjs" "scripts/render-phase-capture.test.mjs": the first pins the labelled, the recorded-edge and the readless subject (AC1-AC3, held-out E2 and E3), and the second re-derives that same edge from the recording and runs the landed join over it. The portal was read for this milestone and carries effect nodes (163 occurrences, one labelled Resource.loadEffect) but renders no panel, so it produces evidence for the wide claim and none for this one. claims.criterionText: The phase an effect ran in is reported as cannot-tell with a named absence, because the page records no effect event: no finding carries a phase for an effect, and no rendered string names rendering or after-render as the phase an effect ran in.
claims.reason: A cannot-tell is a claim, and this one rests on a measurement rather than on an absence of effort: extension/render-phase.js publishes phase as the one constant { state: 'cannot-tell', absence: 'no-effect-event' } outside every finding, and the phrase the criterion forbids - naming rendering or after-render as the phase an effect ran in - appears in neither the join nor the pane. The evidence is the installed profiler enum: 26 values in both @angular/core installs (the panel's and the fixture's), none of them an effect event, which scripts/render-phase-capture.test.mjs derives from the two debug chunks on every run. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/render-phase.test.mjs" "scripts/panel-render-phase.test.mjs" "scripts/render-phase-capture.test.mjs" (held-out E4, T002 AC4, T003 AC2). CHARTER.md's portal clause does not reach the criterion: the portal sweep T001 recorded (8 routes under effect.portalRead, 0 nodes of kind afterRenderEffectPhase and 0 nodes carrying a phase field) produces the absence, not a phase, so a portal-backed verdict could only restate the same cannot-tell. claims.criterionText: A captured NG0100 message produces its own change-detection finding carrying the code and the message the page emitted, and is never joined to an effect, and never presented as evidence that an effect ran during rendering.
claims.reason: This is the criterion whose expected capture does not exist, and the claim says so instead of filling the gap: no page emitted an ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenChecked message at this head, so the change-detection finding is built from the one NG0100 entry of extension/error-digest.json and the recording marks it kind 'digest-entry' with notACapture true and records both attempts as negative with empty messages. The join keeps it as its own finding, after the effect and never merged with it, and the pane renders it as its own block carrying only the code, the message and the provenance it was handed (held-out E5, E6; T002 AC6, T003 AC3). The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/render-phase.test.mjs" "scripts/panel-render-phase.test.mjs" "scripts/render-phase-capture.test.mjs". A portal route was tried for exactly this criterion - 9 route loads across /home, /contract, /claim, /complaint, /customer, /contract/list, /claim/list and /customer/list on the zoneful portal worktree - and produced no NG0100 either, so CHARTER.md's portal clause has nothing to reach here: the artefact both targets lack is the message itself, and the substitute names that. claims.criterionText: Where the graph carries no effect node, or cannot be read at all, the module reports cannot-tell naming which of the two it was, rather than reporting that the page has no effects.
claims.reason: The three absences are published constants, not prose, and the distinction the criterion demands is the one the module keeps: graph-unreadable for a fact that names no readable graph, no-effect-node for a readable graph that holds no node of kind 'effect', and effect-unreadable for a subject the graph does not hold - with the words 'no effects' appearing nowhere in the module's output, so an unread graph is never reported as an empty one (held-out E1, T002 AC5). The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/render-phase.test.mjs", whose AC5 and E1 cases drive all three reasons and assert the forbidden phrase's absence from every answer. CHARTER.md's portal clause does not reach it: the states are a property of the join over a graph it is handed, a portal route's graph is one more fact of the same shape, and no portal page renders the answer - so no portal-backed verdict can add to a check that already runs both absences against measured graphs. claims.criterionText: The panel renders the effect, the signals it reads, the phase state and the change-detection finding as separate things, and renders nothing it was not given.
claims.reason: The pane is a pure view of the join's answer and this is the criterion that forbids it merging the parts: apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-render-phase.ts turns each finding into its own block in the join's order, prints the phase block from phase.state and phase.absence without a constant of its own, prints nothing a finding did not carry, and renders an unwritten state as the word it was given (held-out E7; T003 AC1-AC4). The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-render-phase.test.mjs" "scripts/panel-routes.test.mjs" "scripts/after-render-fixture.test.mjs" plus npx nx run angular-ai-devtools:test, which holds the demo's sample fact to the recording and every rendered line to the join's answer. CHARTER.md's portal clause does not reach it: the panel is the extension's DevTools surface, its route table is apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/app.routes.ts, and no insurance-portal route serves or renders it - the portal is inspected by the panel, never the other way round.
